FdqImhKL29c.body: A two-and-a-half-minute walk through our abrasive belt plant in Xianning, Hubei. The camera follows one belt from raw material to a sealed carton: jumbo rolls of abrasive cloth arriving and being checked, the roll moving onto the converting line, grain and backing confirmed against the order, then slitting, joint making and hot pressing. Later shots cover measurement and quality checking at the end of the line, finished endless belts stacked for dispatch, and the warehouse holding standard sizes for immediate shipment. For buyers comparing suppliers, the useful part is the middle: converting is done in-house, so the spec you confirm in the quotation is the spec that comes off the line.
bullets: Raw material handling and production start
Finished endless belts ready for shipment
Warehouse with abundant stock of abrasive rolls

CJGV6qn3Rf0.body: A full company profile rather than a single production stage. It covers the factory campus including the solar-panel rooftop, the converting halls, the quality area and the finished-goods warehouse, then states the commercial terms plainly: factory-direct pricing, consistent industrial-grade quality, custom sizes, OEM and private label, and delivery from stock. Watch it as an orientation video before you send a specification — it shows what the plant does and does not do, which is the fastest way to avoid a mismatched enquiry.

bf5WPCu6HZs.body: The brand-level introduction to MoTai: who we are, where we make abrasives, and what durable means in practice on a shop floor. Short and useful for partners who need a clip to send onward. The footage covers the production facility, the team at work, and the finished product range, with the standard line we hold to on every order — grain, backing and dimensions confirmed before the run.

ZrYsB2XuR3o.body: An eight-second warehouse shot with one point: we hold stock of standard sizes. Thousands of abrasive cloth rolls and wide abrasive belts sit racked and ready, which is what makes short-lead-time delivery possible for distributors replenishing standard SKUs. If your requirement is a standard width and grit, this is the stock that ships; custom sizes run to the confirmed specification instead.

sdJ-zq2HfjU.body: A single-take tour of the abrasive cloth and belt facility, exterior first and then inside: the production campus, the warehouse with large-format rolls and heavy-duty belts, and a close-up of the cloth backing and grain on a finished belt. The walk-through follows the same order as our manufacturing steps — cutting and converting, sample checks, packing — so it doubles as a practical checklist when you prepare a first enquiry.
bullets: Warehouse: large-format rolls and heavy belts
Product close-up: cloth backing and grain

xBcmPjN7um4.body: Our location in one paragraph: Tongcheng County, Hubei — the abrasive cloth town of China and the central production base for ultra-wide belts. Founded in 2021, the plant cuts the master roll, slits to width, hot presses and cures, then checks, packs and ships. This video explains what ultra-wide means for your application: single-piece belts above 1500 mm without a joint to fail, which is what wide-belt grinding and calibration lines need.

rNbh9PMX-Pw.body: The same one-stop model, stated as a process: we cut the master roll, slit it to your width, hot press and cure the joint, then check and pack. Made in the town that makes abrasive cloth, which matters for lead time on custom widths. Useful if you are deciding between buying converted belts locally and buying slit-to-size from the converting source.

r0AXUY5EEC8.body: Flap discs in a fabrication context: grinding welds, stripping rust, blending and finishing metal parts. The clip shows the construction we supply — aluminum oxide cloth flaps over a backing plate — and the handling points that decide disc life: a flap disc matched to the tool's rated speed, with the guard fitted and the disc presented flat rather than pressed on its edge. For bulk buyers, the practical note is that flap quality and adhesive cure are visible in this footage.
bullets: Where flap discs fit in fabrication
Aluminum oxide flaps over a backing plate
Bulk supply for workshops and distributors

oAEfepQPN3U.body: A converting-line clip: wide abrasive cloth on the conveyor, precision slitting taking the roll down to width, and the serrated or wave-cut edge coming out clean and uniform. Short, but it answers a question that decides fit — whether the edge is cut in-house at the same plant that makes the cloth, rather than outsourced. Custom widths follow from this step.
bullets: Cloth feeding onto the converting line

Iir75GWmjy4.body: Sanding sponge blocks straight from the plant: flexible, double-sided, multi-grit and die-cut to your shape. The demo shows the failure modes that matter — a block bent without cracking, and no grain shedding on the workpiece — plus the custom die-cutting that lets you offer your own profiles. Relevant if you are building a private-label hand-sanding range rather than selling plain stock sheets.
bullets: Die-cut to your profile and packaging

NeE6wfbE-p0.body: A two-minute repair filmed in one shot: find the scratch on the painted wall, work the sponge block over it gently, then touch up. The point for buyers is the grit choice — fine grade only, light pressure, and you are blending a mark rather than removing a coating. An abrasive sponge block is the correct tool here; a hard disc will cut through the paint around the scratch.
bullets: Locate and mark the damaged area

EaXFhDu-8Ic.body: One hook-and-loop disc across four jobs: polishing an epoxy river table, stripping rust and old paint from metal, prepping drywall and putty, and fine detail work on small parts and jewellery. The through-line is dust extraction — the perforated pattern is there to keep the surface clean so you can see when the scratch is gone, which is the actual reason to choose a dustless disc over a solid one.

UL8ERdNJJpo.body: A short tour through the cloth-roll and coated-abrasive plant, from line to finished warehouse, with the commercial points you would ask on a first call: in-house production with quality control, custom specifications, and OEM output. If you need rolls slit to a non-standard width or packed under your own label, this is the footage to watch before writing the brief.

eGdOrKtmgAQ.body: Workshop ASMR: an operator smoothing weld beads on a fabricated steel enclosure with an angle grinder, sparks coming off clean. No narration, but it is a good reference for disc selection — weld removal needs a flap or grinding disc rated for the tool's speed, with the guard in place and the disc presented flat to the work rather than on its edge.

IjZBfRGDyys.body: Thirty seconds from the end of the line to a sealed export carton: cartons wrapped and palletised, racking holding stock, the control screen running the line, and abrasive cloth moving through the roller. The clip covers the four things that go wrong in transit — pack quantity, carton marks, pallet pattern and moisture — which is why we settle them in the quotation rather than at the shipping door.

OQsS-o8DPfU.body: The hot press stage with nothing else in shot: heat and pressure applied until the joint holds under load instead of letting go on a running machine. It is the step most buyers never see and the one that decides whether a belt lasts or fails. If you have had belts open at the joint, this footage answers the question that matters — where is the joint made, and how.
bullets: Heat and pressure on the joint

BZyB_1HKcZw.body: A private-label run end to end in twenty-three seconds: slitting jumbo rolls to your width, checking grade and backing, then packing under the customer's own label before export. For OEM buyers the useful detail is the checkpoint order — spec confirmation, then label and print check, then packing list, so a wrong label is caught before the carton is sealed rather than after it lands.
bullets: Slitting to your width and length

QC5dm0_jJnY.body: Field footage, no studio: an operator taking down weld and mill scale along the edge of a heavy steel plate with a flap disc. It shows the working angle, the pressure, and how fast the disc loads on mill scale — which is the difference between a disc that lasts a shift and one that glazes. Real conditions, which is more useful for specifying grit than a catalogue photo.

kyI_1bAajAE.body: Where bulk orders take shape: slitting jumbo rolls, measuring custom widths, grade-by-grade warehouse stock, and export packing. Twenty-three seconds that cover the whole chain for cloth and roll orders — the part to watch if you buy jumbo rolls and slit in-house, because width tolerance and edge condition are what you inherit from us.

x0tj59ovgBw.body: The automated flap disc line and what the discs are built for: weld finishing and surface preparation in metal fabrication. It covers the supply side too — distributors and importers, workshops and fabrication shops — and the specification order we work to: grit, backing, diameter and arbor hole confirmed together, because a disc that fits nothing is the most common enquiry fault.

XfIphLNhZuk.body: 中文短片：面向工业采购的百叶轮批量供应。自研百叶片配合全自动产线，用于金属打磨、焊缝处理与工件表面预处理，现货发货并支持大批量与 OEM 贴牌。片中可见百叶片的叠层结构、背板装配与下线检验，适合用来判断百叶轮是否耐磨、不掉片。

ePTtos61dbE.body: 一支片子讲清百叶轮的用法与做法：焊缝打磨、木材去毛刺的实拍开场，接背胶、砂布裁切叠层、热压固化全流程，最后看成品是否耐磨、不掉片。对采购方来说，片中叠层与热压两段就是百叶轮寿命的来源，也可作为选择粒度与背板时的参照。
